resources.string: Allows Amply (1) to detect volume buttons and foreground-window package changes so it can show the correct volume controls. It does not read window content or collect or transmit data.
Amply gives you a cleaner volume panel and puts the controls you use most within easy reach.
Let Amply use your volume buttons
Android calls this Accessibility access. Amply uses it to notice volume-button presses and show your volume panel.
Amply doesn’t read what’s on your screen, type for you, or collect your personal data.
Some newer phones ask you to trust sideloaded apps first. Open Amply’s app info, tap the menu in the top-right, then choose “Allow restricted settings.” Come back here when you’re done.
Shizuku unlocks Amply’s per-app volume controls. It’s optional, and you can add it later from the Access tab.
Without Shizuku, Amply still handles your regular Android volume. Per-app controls won’t be available.
Shizuku is connected. Per-app volume controls are ready.
Call awareness helps Amply recognize when your phone is ringing, so your volume buttons stay with the call when it matters.
Amply only checks whether a call is ringing or active. It can’t read phone numbers, contacts, or call history.
Notifications keep Amply’s status and quick pause or retry actions close at hand.
Amply only sends its own status and control notifications. You can change this later in Android settings.
You’re all set! Try it now
Press volume up or volume down. When Amply appears, we’ll show you around.
Amply couldn’t show the panel that time. Check that Accessibility is still enabled, then press a volume button again.
The active stream, percentage, and dot rail show exactly where your volume is. Try tapping or dragging the rail.
Tap the control at the top to mute this stream. Ring controls cycle through the safe ringer modes available on your phone.
The icon identifies the current stream. Tap the expand control to reveal the rest of Amply.
Adjust media, ring, alarm, and notifications independently. Tap another rail to make it the current stream.
When Shizuku is connected, active apps appear here with their own volume controls. This demo uses sample apps only.
Pause when you need the stock controls
The pause button temporarily stands Amply down. The real overlay also dismisses itself after you stop interacting. Keep experimenting here for as long as you like.
Check Accessibility, optional permissions, and Shizuku here. You can also replay this tour whenever you like.
Apps you’ve heard appear here. Save defaults and pin favorites for the expanded overlay; live per-app control needs Shizuku.
Choose the physical side, vertical position, and volume-dot scale that feel best on your phone.
Pause Amply temporarily or let chosen apps receive the stock Android volume keys instead.
Press a volume button, revisit the overlay demo, and tour Amply’s main tabs again.
A new signed APK is available on GitHub Releases. Review what changed before installing it.
Don’t show the connection warning in the volume overlay when Shizuku disconnects.
Keep the expanded overlay focused on Android’s system volume streams.
Remove the red temporary-pause button from the expanded overlay.
Add a DND shortcut to the expanded overlay and extend the ring-volume steps from silent into DND. Android will ask for Do Not Disturb access.
